Tailcat server

Source: R/server.R
TailcatServer.Rd

A tailcat server registers with a public relay and publishes a secret, shareable address. Clients holding the address can dial the ports the server listens on, over TCP or UDP, without accounts or port forwarding.

Blocking methods have an _async() counterpart that returns a promises::promise() resolving with the same value, or rejecting with the same condition. Asynchronous results are delivered by the later event loop, so they only arrive while R is idle at the console, inside Shiny or httpuv, or while you call later::run_now(). The result goes to the loop that was current when the operation started, so an operation started inside later::with_temp_loop() or later::with_loop() completes while that loop runs. If that loop is destroyed before the operation completes, the result is delivered on the global loop instead (checked about once a second while such operations are pending). A pending asynchronous operation can be canceled with tailcat_cancel().

Blocking methods can be interrupted (Ctrl-C or Esc), which cancels the operation. If the operation completes at the same moment, its result is returned and that interrupt is dropped rather than losing data such as bytes just read.

The address and the private and pre-shared keys are secrets: anyone with the address can connect. Printing a server never shows them. $address and the address element of $info() are tailcat_secret strings, which print as <redacted> but otherwise behave like the full address (for example with writeLines() or as.character()). The server does not keep the address in an R field, so saving the server object (for example with saveRDS() or save.image()) does not write the address to disk. Handles do not survive serialization: a server restored from a saved session is closed.

Once a server is closed, every method other than $close(), $format(), and $print(), and every field other than $is_closed, raises a tailcat_closed error; nothing is kept from before.

Timeouts

Every blocking method and function of this package takes a timeout in seconds. Inf waits indefinitely. timeout = 0 is a non-blocking poll: the call returns what is available right away (for example data already received, or a connection already waiting) and otherwise raises tailcat_timeout at once. This differs from tailcat's C ABI (tailcat.h), where a zero timeout is an already expired deadline that fails without trying; rtailcat gives a poll a deadline of a few milliseconds instead. A poll waits for an operation started before it in the same direction of a connection only for that short time.

A timeout ends only that call: the server, listener, client, or connection stays usable.

Errors

Errors are conditions with class tailcat_error and one subclass that says what went wrong. Each also carries an integer status (the status code of the C ABI) and bytes, the number of bytes transferred before the error (for reads and writes; otherwise 0). The message starts with a one-line summary; a line starting tailcat: gives tailcat's own description when it has one.

statusClassMeaning
1tailcat_invalid_argumentAn argument is invalid
2tailcat_closedThe object, or the client or server that owns it, is closed
3tailcat_timeoutThe timeout ran out
4tailcat_canceledThe operation was canceled with tailcat_cancel()
5tailcat_failureAnything else, including calls made in the wrong state

Branch on the class (for example with tryCatch(..., tailcat_timeout = function(e) ...)) or the status, not on the message, whose wording may change.

Operations in flight

Every operation that can block (each method or function with a timeout, and fields such as $address that ask tailcat), synchronous or asynchronous, holds its own operating system thread from the moment it starts until it ends, including while it waits its turn behind other reads or writes on a connection. The option rtailcat.max_operations caps how many such operations may be in flight in the R process at once. It must be a single positive whole number, or Inf for no cap, and defaults to 1024, which stays well below the per-process thread limits of macOS (about 6,000) and typical Linux systems and the 10,000 threads at which the Go runtime ends the process. The option is read each time an operation starts. An operation started when the cap is reached fails at once with a tailcat_failure error that names the option and gives the limit, without affecting the operations already in flight; once some of them finish or are canceled, new operations work again. If the option is set to an invalid value, every such operation fails with a tailcat_failure error saying so.

Active bindings

address

The secret tailcat address to give to clients, as a tailcat_secret. It is fetched from tailcat on each access (a quick local call) rather than stored in R. Errors if the server has not started.

public_key

The server's public key, or NA before the server has started.

is_started

TRUE once the server has started (registered with the relay), FALSE before.

is_closed

TRUE once the server has been closed.

TailcatServer$new()

Create a server. Nothing is sent over the network until the server is started (by $start() or $listen()). Only arguments that are not NULL are passed to tailcat.

Usage

TailcatServer$new(
  key = NULL,
  preshared_key = NULL,
  region_id = NULL,
  region = NULL,
  derp_map_url = NULL,
  allowed_clients = NULL,
  udp_idle_timeout = NULL
)

Arguments

key

Private node key: a string in tailcat's text encoding, a tailcat_keys object from tailcat_keygen(), or NULL to generate one. A tailcat_keys object also supplies the pre-shared key, unless preshared_key is given. Keep the keys to reuse an address across restarts.

preshared_key

Pre-shared key (text encoding), or NULL to generate one (or take it from key).

region_id

Integer relay region to register in, or NULL to choose automatically.

region

A relay region definition, as a list or a JSON string, to use instead of the public relay map. Field names may be the snake_case names used by tailcat_address_parse() (region_id, region_code, nodes, and within each node name, host_name, ipv4, relay_port, and so on) or the PascalCase names of Tailscale's DERPRegion type (RegionID, Nodes, HostName, DERPPort, and so on).

derp_map_url

URL of a relay map to use instead of the default.

allowed_clients

Character vector of client public keys. If given, only these clients may connect; otherwise anyone with the address may.

udp_idle_timeout

Seconds after which an idle UDP flow is dropped, or NULL for the default.

TailcatServer$start()

Register with the relay so the server has an address. Calling it again is harmless.

Usage

TailcatServer$start(timeout = 30)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls (see the section on timeouts).

Returns

The server, invisibly.

Arguments

timeout

Returns

A promise resolving with the server.

TailcatServer$listen()

Listen on a port, starting the server first if needed.

Usage

TailcatServer$listen(port = 0L, network = c("tcp", "udp"), timeout = 30)

Arguments

port

Port number; 0 picks a free port (see the listener's $port).

network

Exactly "tcp" (the default) or "udp".

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A TailcatListener.

TailcatServer$listen_async()

Asynchronous version of $listen().

Usage

TailcatServer$listen_async(port = 0L, network = c("tcp", "udp"), timeout = 30)

Arguments

port

Port number; 0 picks a free port.

network

Exactly "tcp" (the default) or "udp".

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A promise resolving with a TailcatListener.

TailcatServer$allow_client()

Add a client public key to the allowlist. Once the list has an entry, only listed clients can register; existing connections are not affected.

Usage

Arguments

public_key

A client public key, for example TailcatClient$public_key.

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

The server, invisibly.

TailcatServer$info()

Information about the started server.

Usage

TailcatServer$info(timeout = 30)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A list of class tailcat_info (so that format() redacts the address in every version of R) with address (a tailcat_secret), ip (the server's own IP address on the tailcat network, without a port), and public_key. Errors if the server has not started.

TailcatServer$drain()

Wait for TCP shutdown traffic to finish. Call it after closing connections and before closing the server or exiting R, so that peers see a clean end of stream.

Usage

TailcatServer$drain(timeout = 5)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait. Inf is accepted but waits as long as shutdown takes, which can be indefinitely when a peer has gone away, so a finite value is recommended.

Returns

The server, invisibly.

TailcatServer$drain_async()

Asynchronous version of $drain().

Usage

TailcatServer$drain_async(timeout = 5)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; as for $drain(), a finite value is recommended.

Returns

A promise resolving with the server.

TailcatServer$close()

Close the server, its listeners, and all of its connections. Pending operations on them end with a tailcat_closed error. Closing twice is harmless. Closing tears the server down immediately, so clients may not see the end of their streams until their own reads time out; to give clients a clean end of stream, close the connections and call $drain() first.

Usage

TailcatServer$close()

Returns

The server, invisibly.

TailcatServer$format()

Format a summary, the lines that $print() shows. The address and keys are never shown. A closed server shows only its state.

Usage

TailcatServer$format(...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

Returns

A character vector.

TailcatServer$print()

...

Ignored.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
srv = TailcatServer$new()
lst = srv$listen(8080)
srv$address # share this with the client, it is a secret
conn = lst$accept()
conn$read()
srv$close()
} # }
